claims.text: LangChain's paid-media agent runs a recurring Monday Slack workflow that joins advertising data to warehouse leads/pipeline and produces platform-specific reports, and users can request analysis and campaign changes.

LangChain's paid-media agent is built on general-purpose Deep Agents and LangSmith infrastructure with bespoke advertising tools and playbooks; scheduled reporting delegates to platform-specific subagents, each request gets an isolated sandbox/checkpoint, and calculations and hard safeguards are code rather than model judgment.

In LangChain's paid-media agent, only designated Slack user IDs can edit or approve campaign changes; approval cards show current and proposed values, and code executes approved changes and verifies success on the advertising platform.

LangChain reports paid media rose from 0% to 20% of marketing pipeline in six months, cost per qualified lead fell 30% from June to August while monthly spend rose about 60%, and in-house reporting saved about $5,000/month; these are team-reported before/after outcomes, not a controlled attribution study.
Moving calculations into code and removing unnecessary model calls made an early LangChain reporting workflow about 40x cheaper and 13x faster (18 minutes to 85 seconds).
A LangChain paid-media failure: two subagents shared an output location and completion flag so one platform's report suppressed another's; the fix separated their files and completion state.

A LangChain paid-media agent repeatedly checked whether its PDF rendered, consuming excessive tokens and trying to rebuild it; the fix restricted it to read-context, compute and render tools and treated successful rendering as completion.

When cross-platform data cannot be joined reliably, LangChain's paid-media agent reports source, date window and attribution model rather than filling gaps; Slack proved awkward for complex bulk edits, prompting a dedicated interface.

LangChain's GTM agent, built on general-purpose Deep Agents and LangSmith, does Salesforce-triggered lead research and personalized outreach using isolated subagents with constrained tool sets, structured output contracts, and a virtual filesystem for large tool results.

In LangChain's GTM agent, reps get Slack drafts with reasoning and sources and can send, edit or cancel, but a 48-hour SLA for 'silver' leads auto-sends if no approval or rejection occurs, an exception to the initial no-send-without-approval requirement.

LangChain's GTM agent checks recent support issues and prior teammate contact before drafting; CI combines tool/order/duplicate-draft assertions with an LLM judge for tone, length and formatting, and substantive rep edits become per-rep style memories in PostgreSQL.

LangChain reports for December 2025 to March 2026 that lead-to-qualified-opportunity conversion rose 250%, pipeline dollars 3x, and reps reclaimed 40 hours/month each (1,320 hours team-wide); the post does not establish a controlled causal estimate.

Docusign's sales outreach system uses five agents (Identifier, Researcher, Composer, Validator, Orchestrator) inside a deterministic CrewAI Flow that controls sequencing, state and errors, with three validation layers: LLM-as-judge, hallucination checks against source material, and API-based quality scoring.

CrewAI reports faster turnaround and higher open, reply and conversion rates for Docusign but publishes no numerical uplift or explicit human approval gate; the '14x less code' figure in the article concerns another customer.

7-Eleven's marketing creative assistant is a custom application on LangGraph and Databricks with campaign creative generator, copywriter, general assistant, supervisor and web-search agents; the supervisor routes work and reviews quality.

7-Eleven's system allows live UI interruptions and email reviews for human approval at any stage, applies brand-voice configuration, and runs toxicity, PII and off-policy filters, with MLflow tracing and evaluation of groundedness, safety and relevance.

7-Eleven reports multi-channel concepts and scripts that took hours or days can be generated, refined and approved in minutes, but discloses no campaign lift or numerical labor savings; automated execution and image/video features are roadmap items.

Bonterra uses two custom agents in Jasper Grid, a categorizer labeling reviews by sentiment, rating and content type and a response generator with conditional rules, with Jasper IQ enforcing brand voice and flagging edge cases for human review.

Bonterra reports review responses taking under two hours versus at least 12 hours before (83% reduction) and monthly batches of about 40 reviews handled in under two minutes; whether every public response receives human sign-off is not specified.

PGA TOUR's Automated Content System uses research, writer, validation, editor and multimedia agents on Amazon Bedrock; validators extract factual claims into fact tables, verify them against authoritative sources and trigger writer revisions on discrepancies.

PGA TOUR reports about 1,200+ content pieces per week at under $0.25 per piece and a 95% cost reduction, but does not document mandatory human sign-off before publication or name a reusable orchestration framework.

Gradial, a commercial domain-specific agent platform on AWS, uses different models per task (Nova for authoring/AEM updates, Nova Act for simulated buyer journeys, Claude for QA/governance/optimization); AWS reports up to 20x efficiency gains and 99.9% content-operation accuracy for AWS and T-Mobile without publishing the test definition or an approval gate.

BlueOceanAI Spark decomposes marketer questions into subquestions for specialist agents with dataset access, using Amazon Bedrock and unnamed open-source multi-agent frameworks; AWS reports 1.2 billion tokens and 10,000+ questions in the first month, tasks falling from about five days to two hours, and 66-96% lower customer analytics costs.

Morgan Stanley's FIXR reconciliation agents turn repeated controller resolutions into durable rules, auto-clear known breaks and flag unfamiliar ones for controllers to approve or correct; reconciliation fell from up to six hours to two to three hours and about 1,500 hours saved weekly across roughly 100 controllers, with framework, error rate and auto-clear share undisclosed.

Bertelsmann's Content Search is a production LangGraph system routing natural-language queries to specialist agents across existing book, documentary and news systems and synthesizing answers; discovery fell from hours to seconds, with no numerical benchmark disclosed.
